root_cause.text: The Btrfs filesystem lacks an early check for directory item overflow caused by name hash collisions during file creation, resulting in a transaction abort and a read-only filesystem when the leaf size limit is exceeded after tree updates have already begun.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a call to `btrfs_check_dir_item_collision()` at the beginning of `btrfs_create_new_inode()` before any tree updates or path allocations occur, avoiding a transaction abort when a new name cannot be added due to leaf size limits.

intent_record.intent_summary: Check for directory item collisions before creating a new inode to avoid transaction aborts.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional block at the start of btrfs_create_new_inode to call btrfs_check_dir_item_collision when creating non-orphan, non-subvolume inodes.
intent_record.how: It prevents transaction aborts by verifying early that adding the new directory entry will not cause an overflow due to name hash collisions.

grouping_result.intent: Check for directory item collisions before creating a new inode to avoid transaction aborts.

relevance_review.reason: The group's core intent is to check for directory item collisions before creating a new inode to avoid transaction aborts, which directly addresses the vulnerability root cause of lacking an early check for directory item overflow caused by name hash collisions.

candidates.rationale: The vulnerability is due to the lack of an early check for directory item overflow (hash collision) before starting transaction updates. This check needs to be performed after allocating the path, which is used to search for the collision.
The early check for directory item overflow is missing immediately after the path allocation and its successful validation.
